title: Date 'year != 0' guard is dead code; comment misrepresents the check
description: header_typed.rs:259 guards: HeaderValue::DateTime(dt) if dt.year != 0 && dt.month != 0 && dt.day != 0. The comment on lines 256-258 claims this is 'belt-and-braces: also reject all-zero year/month/day'. But mail_parser's parse_date (date.rs:416-422) maps parts[2] in 0..=49 to year+2000 — so dt.year is never 0 from a real parse. The year!=0 branch is dead. The month and day guards still filter genuinely all-zero outputs (parser reaches pos>=6 with no day/month digits). Either remove the dead year!=0 check and update the comment, or document precisely which inputs the guard catches. Trigger: cosmetic; no user-visible bug, but the comment is wrong and a future maintainer will copy this pattern thinking year==0 is a real failure mode.
close_reason: Code cleanup batch: (.3) removed dead 'year != 0' guard in date arm and replaced comment with accurate description of what month/day == 0 catches (year mapping in mail-parser-0.11 means parts[2] is never 0 after remap); (.21) eliminated unreachable! by folding Raw and URLs handling into the same outer match as the other forms — no top-level if-and-then-match anymore; (.22) replaced split_last + unwrap_or_else with straightforward slice arithmetic via a new crlf_terminated helper returning Cow; (.23) extracted trim_or_none helper for the RFC 8621 §4.1.2.3/§4.1.2.4 display-name normalisation rule, called from both convert_addr and group_addresses.
